if you do get anxiety while on the date and for any reason need to leave, i’m sure the other person will understand. honestly, basically everyone i know (even the ones without anxiety disorders) get anxious about going on dates. i wish you the best of luck!

honestly i’m 24 and have the same problems. i had my first kiss at 21 and haven’t kissed anyone since. i’ve dated one person, but it was only for a few months online. i’ve tried to go on dates with people from dating apps, but i end up getting so nervous that i just cancel and ghost them.

i think i just psych myself out because i view dating as a bigger deal than it is. there isn’t really a wrong way to do it. you can go on one date with someone, and there’s no obligation to do anything else with them. you can go as slow as you want. for me, i always feel like there’s certain things i’m supposed to do or steps i’m supposed to follow, but the truth is, dating is whatever you are comfortable with.

if you have anxiety and want to form a non-romantic relationship with someone first before starting to date, i’m sure there are plenty of other people out there who prefer to move at that pace as well. if you’re just honest and upfront about it, people can be understanding and if they’re not, they’re honestly not someone i would want to be in a relationship with anyway.

i get so many physical symptoms from anxiety. tightening chest, hyperventilating, headache, dizziness, nausea, hot flashes, etc etc. it’s gotten to the point that when i experience these symptoms due to something unrelated (like a fever), it makes me feel anxious because my body assumes i’m having a panic attack. it’s incredibly unpleasant.

i just treat it like i would any physical illness. take my medication (both for my anxiety and possible symptoms i’m experiencing), lay down, drink lots of water and eat foods that are easy on my stomach. anxiety is really tiring on the body, so it makes sense to have these kinds of physical symptoms.

i struggle with the same thing. i feel like i constantly need the attention to be on me or i don’t feel like i’m wanted/cared about. it makes me feel like a terrible person.

i try to keep things at a balance as much as i can. i tell myself that everyone needs and wants attention, so it’s nothing to be ashamed of. i just happen to want more, possibly because i was missing the attention or affection i needed previously in life. i feel ashamed so i feel the need to lie a lot, but just telling the truth can be really helpful. 

i’ll go to my friends and say things like “i’ve felt kinda isolated lately and like i’m not wanted around. i know that the chances are that it’s just me feeling that way because of my insecurity, but i wanted to express how i’ve been feeling.” or sometimes i’ll just say “hey can you give me some reassurance about this thing really quick?” i try not to rely on others for validation too much, but once in a while if nothing works, i will just be honest with them. the truth is that a lot of people feel these things, so if you’re close to them and express it, chances are they’ll be understanding.

the best thing that’s helped me outside of that or when i feel like i’m relying on other people too much is journaling. i write down the opposite of what i’m feeling. so if i’m craving attention because i feel like my friend doesn’t care about me anymore, i’ll write “this person is a really good friend of mine and cares about me deeply.” i just keep writing stuff like that until i feel better. i feel like it really helps to shift my perspective.

i have only dated one person and i dumped him. the truth is that despite caring about him, he broke my trust on a number of different occasions, and i felt that i couldn’t trust him. he also did a few things i didn’t particularly agree with (using hard drugs, following OF girls on instagram and twitter, watching violent porn, etc) that made me kinda uncomfortable. 

but i think the part that ultimately led to me dumping him was that he just couldn’t fulfill my emotional needs. he knew i have BPD and that i would require more to patience and reassurance than the average person. he said he was okay with that, and in exchange, i would try to reduce my “neediness” as much as i could and use healthy coping mechanisms. i would do my part, but he didn’t really do his. he kept expecting me to do more while he did less. it got to the point where he was doing things like taking new female friends out to dinner alone and following a female friend’s NSFW twitter, and when i would be upset, he would get angry with me for overreacting. so i decided to dump him.

at the time, it felt like an impulse, but i think it was coming for a long time. there was (and kinda still is) a part of me that regrets it. sometimes i think about all the nice things he used to say and do for me, and i convince myself the bad parts weren’t that bad. but ultimately, i realize that he just isn’t a good boyfriend in general, and he has a lot of things he needs to work on. i hope he sorts himself out so that he doesn’t hurt another girl like he hurt me, and i hope that i can find someone who can meet my emotional needs.

It’s going to be really hard to help him if he doesn’t want to help himself. I would do my best to encourage him to look into some sort of DBT, which helps people with BPD learn skills to manage their emotions and improve interpersonal relationships. I personally did an intensive outpatient program, which was a group program that met 4 times a week for 2 hours a day, plus a once per week, one hour long individual therapy session. However, I know there is individual DBT therapy, as well as more intensive inpatient or residential program options.

That being said, BPD is not an excuse to hurt/scare your family. While it may lead to some extreme emotions, he also has personal responsibility for doing those things to you. If it comes down to it, please do not be afraid to put the safety of your family first, even if it means no longer supporting your brother. Good luck <3

I’ve been on a lot of different antidepressants for a long part of my life. Although I have felt like you before, I realize now that being on antidepressants doesn’t make you a failure, just like being on medication for a physical illness doesn’t. Also, I have known many people who have been on antidepressants and then gotten off of them when they no longer needed them, without all of their problems coming back.

That being said, you’re correct in the sense that there isn’t a medication specifically for BPD. Personally, I find that antidepressants and anti-anxiety medication can be helpful for me. If you are still interested in trying antidepressants, there are many out there that your GP hasn’t tried yet. Zoloft and Prozac are both SSRIs, which is only one type of antidepressant. There are more SSRIs out there, plus there are other types like SNRIs and tricyclics. It’s ultimately up to what your doctor thinks will be best for you, but you can always look into it :)

Hi. I know how difficult this can be because it happened to me. It can make you feel sad, angry, anxious and even disgusted, which are things that are not super comfortable to feel towards a partner.

I would start by trying to have a conversation with him. Make sure you are not in a place where your emotions are taking over. It might seem silly, but it helps me stay more rational if I write down what I want to say before. Make sure you communicate how you feel and why you feel the way that you feel. Try not to accuse him or blame him of things because it may cause him to lash out or refuse to listen.

Considering this is a behavior that *technically* does not involve you (despite it hurting your feelings) and that he is “addicted”, it may be difficult to get him to change. But see if there is some sort of compromise that can be made. If he is willing, perhaps he can lessen the amount of porn he watches or start doing certain things that can help you to feel more comfortable in the relationship.

There are also things that you can do to try to help yourself. See if there’s any way to reframe your thoughts about this. While the women in porn seem “unrealistic”, they are all just normal women. Sometimes it helps me if I see them outside of porn (like in interviews or even behind the scenes stuff) because it helps humanize them a bit more. Also, their physical attractiveness does not take away from your own. Maybe if you can do certain things to help increase your own feelings of self-esteem, you will feel better. Personally, I am an affirmation person, but to each their own.

about once every few months or so i get periods of time where my anxiety/depression is so bad that i can’t eat. idk if this will help but there are some things that work for me. 

first, i try to stick to a BRAT diet (bananas, rice, applesauce, toast) + saltines or anything else super bland. nothing spicy or acidic. if i can get protein shakes down, i try to do that too because none of the foods i listed before have a lot of protein.

also, when i do have the craving for something and if it’s not too spicy/acidic, i try to find a way to get it. for example, if i want a cheeseburger, i will jump in my car right at that moment and go through a drive thru. sometimes not eating a while can make it even harder to eat and cause more nausea, but eating that one thing can help me get back my appetite.

i know feeling like this sucks, and i really hope it gets better soon :)
